text: The robot module lifecycle begins with the initialization phase, configuring the necessary models and controllers before simulation.
A robot model is loaded, defining the kinematic and dynamic properties of the chosen robotic arm.
A gripper model specifies the end-effector geometry and attachment properties for manipulation.
The controller is initialized to define how high-level commands will map into low-level actuation.
During runtime, the robot actively interacts with the simulation environment across each control step.
The central robot abstraction coordinates command execution and state synchronization within the environment.
External policies or input devices supply high-level action commands to the robot.
The internal controller converts these action commands into joint torque values to actuate the physics model.
In response to physical interactions, observations such as camera renderings are generated for the agent.
Finally, callable interfaces allow external programs to access relevant state information at any point.
Specifications expose static properties, limits, and configuration metadata of the robot instance.
Proprioception methods provide direct access to joint positions, velocities, and operational poses.
Sensor callables retrieve measurements from attached devices, including force-torque and contact signals.
